title: cv
text:
Statistician with experience building interpretable models for complex observational data, and the software to fit them at scale. I currently lead the modelling and engineering behind the Biodiversity Intactness Index (BII) in the Biodiversity Futures Lab at the Natural History Museum, London.
I have a PhD in statistics from the University of Western Australia and was a postdoc at the University of Cambridge, where I developed Bayesian methods for combining mechanistic models with data when those models are known to be wrong.

title: cv
text:
Statistical modelling

Inference under model misspecification. Developed the statistical finite element method, a Bayesian framework that embeds a Gaussian process discrepancy term in a mechanistic model so that inference stays honest when the model is wrong.
PNAS, 2021 · paper
Scalable Bayesian computation. Built low-rank approximations and Langevin-based sampling schemes that make posterior inference tractable for high-dimensional models.
J. Comput. Phys., 2022 · paper · SIAM/ASA JUQ, 2022 · paper
Learning from unstructured data. Co-developed physics-informed variational autoencoders that link raw, unstructured observations to interpretable latent dynamics.
J. Comput. Phys., 2024 · paper

title: cv
text:
Experience

Senior Research Software Engineer — Natural History Museum, London (2026–present)

Lead the statistical modelling and technical development of the BII, a global biodiversity indicator built on mixed-effects models from over 4 million observations, from over 35 thousand sites from the PREDICTS database.
Own the model specification, validation, and uncertainty propagation from site-level data to global projections.
Maintain the BII’s R packages and HPC/AWS deployment, and work with ecologists to turn research questions into models.

Research Software Engineer — Natural History Museum, London (2024–2026)

Refactored the BII pipeline into tested R packages and deployed it on HPC.
Scaled projections from 10 km to 1 km resolution.
Published two CRAN packages (predictsr, ssmooth) and added CI, testing, documentation, and QA.

Postdoctoral Research Associate — University of Cambridge (2021–2024)

Recruited to Mark Girolami’s group in the final year of my PhD; completed the thesis alongside the first year of the postdoc.
Developed Bayesian inference methods (MCMC, Langevin dynamics, filtering) for complex physical models, with a focus on model misspecification and uncertainty quantification.
Published in PNAS, SIAM/ASA JUQ, and the Journal of Computational Physics.

Teaching Assistant — University of Western Australia (2018–2020)

Taught undergraduate and master’s statistics courses through tutorials, assessment setting, and exam marking.

title: Starting Up
text:
Hi! This is planned to build up an archive of different things that I find interest related to programming, software development, and computational sciences.
I plan to post things that I find generally interesting in relation to stuff that I’ve worked on in the past, or things that I’ve more recently done, or more general thoughts on the interface of science and software development.

title: Connor Duffin
text:
I’m a statistician who builds interpretable models for messy observational data, along with the software to run them reliably at scale.
At the Natural History Museum in London, I lead the modelling and engineering behind the Biodiversity Intactness Index. This involves hierarchical mixed-effects models fitted to heterogeneous data pooled from many independent field studies, then projected globally.
Before that, I did a PhD in statistics at the University of Western Australia and a postdoc at the University of Cambridge, developing Bayesian methods for combining mechanistic models with data when those models are known to be wrong (PNAS, 2021).

title: software
text: This is a brief portfolio of software development projects I’ve been involved in, including both research software and proprietary software for my current role at the Natural History Museum.

title: software
text:
R packages

predictsr is an R package to load the PREDICTS database into R dataframes and cache them to disk. Published on CRAN.
ssmooth is an R package for smoothing spatial data using statistical methods. Uses C++ for the core smoothing algorithms, and is published on CRAN.

title: software
text:
Selected Proprietary Works

BII codebase (NHM): R packages to ingest, transform, and model the PREDICTS database, which is used to generate the Biodiversity Intactness Index. Using R geospatial stack: terra, sf, lme4, etc.
BII HPC pipeline (NHM): HPC pipelines to generate global biodiversity data for the BII. Using targets and Docker containers, running on AWS EC2.
BII QA pipeline (NHM): generate QA checks for the BII data, including visualisations and summary statistics. Standard geospatial data processing using R geospatial stack: terra, sf, ggplot2, etc.

title: software
text:
Research software

statFEM code to accompany these papers (FEM code is implemented with FEniCS):

The 1D case (including the internal wave experimental data) is housed at statkdv-paper. This code computes the posterior (filtering) distribution using extended and ensemble Kalman filters.
The 2D case is located here. This also computes the posterior filtering distribution using a low-rank extended Kalman filter algorithm.

ula-statfem: code to explore Langevin dynamics samplers with statFEM. Published in SIAM JUQ. Includes sfmcmc package which implements a bunch of different MCMC samplers, including ULA (see this classic paper), MALA, and preconditioned Crank-Nicolson.
statfenics: a set of tools to help when doing statistics with FEniCS. Includes functions to build Gaussian process inference on top of FEniCS, and utilities to aid in interpolating finite element solutions.

title: software
text:
Personal projects

dotfiles for *nix systems that I use day-to-day. I use yadm to manage these files across all the systems I use (e.g., work laptop, HPC). Includes configurations for zsh, tmux, neovim, and more.
uLinalg: a C++ library to handle 2D array operations, including broadcasting, LU decompositions, and Cholesky decompositions. A bit like a mini version of numpy.
pspectral: a C++ library to compute pseudospectral solutions to differential equations, such as Navier-Stokes, using Fourier transforms (FFTW).
punter: a C++ implementation of the Shunting-Yard to parse mathematical expressions from infix to postfix notation.
